claims.text: The operating model rests on three pillars: be profitable, have investors talking to you rather than the other way round, and open source everything.
claims.quote: it rests on three pillars that are easier to state than to do

claims.text: The pillars are in that order for a reason: each one buys the position needed to do the next.
claims.quote: Each one buys you the position you need to do the next.

claims.text: Strip away the mythology and a startup is simple: make a thing somebody wants to buy, at a price that is profitable to you.
claims.quote: You make a thing somebody wants to buy, at a price that is profitable to you.

claims.text: The single most important skill is the ability to ship, every day, because shipping is how you find out what is true.
claims.quote: And ship every day, because shipping is how you find out what is true.

claims.text: Shipping means a thing somebody else can go and use on their own and get value from, not a proof of concept, a demo or a prototype walked through on a call.
claims.quote: It means a thing somebody else can go and use, on their own, and get value from.

claims.text: To ship that often the running cost must be near nothing: serverless, as few databases and as little live state as possible, and in our case the file system is the database.
claims.quote: Serverless. As few databases and as little live state as you can stand.

claims.text: With nothing running between requests, the standing bill for an estate of thirty one published graphs is a third of a gigabyte of object storage.
claims.quote: the standing bill for an estate of thirty one published graphs is a third of a gigabyte of object storage

value.unit: published graphs held in a third of a gigabyte of object storage

claims.text: Getting a working thing into a stranger's hands is still hard in 2026, and solving that is not overhead but the first real product you build.
claims.quote: Solving that is not overhead, it is the first real product you build.

claims.text: Hand the product to people for free, for a short window, so the feedback loop is tight and the cost of generosity stays inside what you can absorb.
claims.quote: Not forever: a short window, whatever unit makes sense, but short.

claims.text: Giving it away solves dozens of problems you did not know you had, because the feedback starts the moment somebody who is not you has the thing.
claims.quote: The feedback starts the moment somebody who is not you has the thing.

claims.text: Then take it away, with nothing else about the product changed and no apology, and ask the only question that matters: do they miss it?
claims.quote: Take it away. The trial expired. It is not available right now.

claims.text: If they shrug, you have something people accept when it is free, which is a weak signal; no sense of loss means no why now, and without a why now there is nothing to sell.
claims.quote: No sense of loss means no why now, and without a why now there is nothing to sell.

claims.text: Can you charge, and can you charge at a profit? Two questions, and people routinely answer only the first.
claims.quote: Two questions, and people routinely answer only the first.

claims.text: Revenue comes first: if you cannot get revenue at all, that is the problem to solve, and it is not a marketing problem.
claims.quote: If you cannot get revenue at all, that is the problem to solve, and it is not a marketing problem.

claims.text: Do not reach for a subscription by default: a subscription is a discount for regular use, not rent on something somebody ignores, and pay on demand is usually healthier.
claims.quote: a subscription is a discount for regular use, not rent on something somebody ignores

claims.text: The worst possible time to raise money is before you are profitable, before the product and before the fit, which is exactly when most companies raise.
claims.quote: The worst possible time to raise money is before you are profitable

claims.text: Profitability means time as well as money: when you are not bleeding you can wait, and being able to wait is most of a good negotiating position.
claims.quote: being able to wait is most of what a good negotiating position is

claims.text: Handing a say in the business to investors whose focus is structurally misaligned is one of the most common ways companies fail, and it is self-inflicted at signing.
claims.quote: I think that is one of the most common ways companies fail

claims.text: The analogy is music: do not get signed before you have the album; write, record, play locally, get people buying, then take the deal as somebody with an audience.
claims.quote: Do not get signed before you have the album.

claims.text: Pillar two is not never raise: raise from strength, on terms you set, from people who came to you because the thing already works.
claims.quote: Raise from strength, on terms you set, from people who came to you because the thing already works.

claims.text: Open sourcing everything is not giving away the asset, for five reasons, the first being that the technology is not the moat and believing it is shapes every decision badly.
claims.quote: The technology is not the moat.

claims.text: Open source is a better exit for the founder: build in the open and the work is still yours when you move on; you leave with your tools.
claims.quote: Build in the open and the work is still yours when you move on.

claims.text: open-source.sgit.ai carries the longer argument, and its thesis is that open source is a strategy, not a charity.
claims.quote: open source is a strategy, not a charity

claims.text: A follow-up of 2 October 2026, Price it, then give it away, covers the next step and was written when RiskMandate's early access programme went live.
claims.quote: written when RiskMandate's early access programme went live

claims.text: Every pillar asks that shipping a usable product be cheap, fast and reversible, an infrastructure requirement a vault answers: data, app, history and sources travel as one string.
claims.quote: shipping a usable product should be cheap, fast, and reversible

claims.text: The whole published estate is 2,662 files and 295 MB of object storage, with nothing running between questions, opened with a single read key.
claims.quote: is 2,662 files and 295 MB of object storage, with nothing running between questions

value.unit: files in the published estate, 295 MB

claims.text: The loop of shipping, taking away and finding out is the product the author most wants others to have, which is why the whole stack is open source, down to the measurements and the mistakes.
claims.quote: it is why the whole stack is open source, down to the measurements and the mistakes

claims.text: Whether the company makes a profit in a given year is a separate question; the claim is about the product, which does not scale if it is not profitable.
claims.quote: Whether the company makes a profit in a given year is a separate question with its own answer

claims.text: The price might not be profitable today and still be right if the economics clearly improve with scale, as long as the gap can be self funded.
claims.quote: it might not be profitable today and still be the right price, if the economics clearly improve with scale
